page: Amazon Web Services i4i.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C) running at 3.5 GHz across an x86_64 architecture. The server provisions 96 vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 768 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz (an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio). Hardware acceleration includes AVX-512 vector extensions, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic enhancements such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes 22,500 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 56 Gbps, with zero GPUs allocated.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and high-density memory operations alongside average single-core capability. In stress-ng, the multi-core CPU score placed in the top 25% at 92,861.79, while single-core performance sat in the middle 50% at 1,891.49. Similarly, Geekbench multi-core achieved 17,841.0 (top 25%) versus 1,642.0 on a single core. In PassMark tests, CPU encryption landed in the top 10% (87,228.27), bolstered by hardware-level AES instructions, and the extended instructions score reached 85,259.36. Large block memory read bandwidth clocked at 322.22 GB/sec with write throughput at 139.48 GB/sec.

Data-centric transaction testing demonstrates the machine's strengths, achieving 89.14 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 29,810.64 in PassMark database operations, both ranking in the top 25%. However, running large language models reveals CPU-bound execution tradeoffs without hardware accelerators; text generation on a 70B parameter model registers in the bottom 25% at 2.79 tokens/sec, though small 135M model prompt processing reaches 2,413.42 tokens/sec. The instance delivers solid qualitative cost efficiency for organizations that demand dense direct-attached NVMe storage paired with high parallelism, reducing the need to maintain separate storage networks.

The hardware configuration makes Amazon Web Services i4i.24xlarge well suited for I/O-intensive transactional databases, large distributed NoSQL data stores, search indexing engines, real-time analytics clusters, and caching layers requiring immense local storage and memory density.
description: Amazon Web Services i4i.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz. It includes 768 GB of DDR4 memory, 56 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and 22,500 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, with no integrated GPUs. Multi-core compute and data-intensive benchmarks place the instance in the upper quartiles, registering 89.14 million Redis SET operations per second, a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,841.0, and top-tier PassMark encryption performance of 87,228.27 via dedicated cryptographic extensions. While single-thread and unaccelerated large LLM inference capabilities remain average to weak, the massive local NVMe capacity paired with substantial memory density offers strong architectural efficiency for distributed databases, high-throughput NoSQL engines, and intensive transactional analytical processing.
